workflow.title: Thread a reversible webbing closure
workflow.summary: Follow a labelled front/back slot path, expose hidden routing and recover a twist without restarting the whole assembly.
workflow.physicalScope: Non-loadbearing instrument-pouch or bench-fixture webbing prototypes with a known slot path. The result carries no load-retention or personal-support rating.

requiredFacts.label: This is a non-loadbearing webbing prototype, with no personal-support or secure-load claim.
Exact slot order and front/back path from the reference design
Actual labels on every slot and the fixed or free webbing end
Physical mark identifying the webbing front face and fixture front
Measured webbing width for this prototype
Minimum free tail length required by the reference design
Permitted threading/pulling actions and available hands or supports

steps.title: Identify the path and the two faces
steps.instruction: Show the slot labels and face marks. Resolve the entry slot and the next front/back transition before asking the operator to thread anything.
visibleChecks: The active entry slot label is legible.
The marked webbing face and fixture face are distinguishable.
The shown entry corresponds to the declared slot path.

requiredConfirmations.label: This is a non-loadbearing prototype and the reference path is the intended design.
I identified the real front/back marks and the free webbing end.

steps.recoveryHint: Add visible face marks or expose the entry slot. Do not substitute an assumed over/under pattern for an unreadable reference.

steps.title: Thread the next constrained segment
steps.instruction: Check one entry/exit pair at a time. Guide the free end through its next declared slot while keeping the marked face consistent.
visibleChecks: The current entry and exit slot are visible.
The active segment follows the declared local slot order.
The visible webbing face does not show an unexplained half twist.

requiredConfirmations.label: I physically checked the threaded slot sequence, including the current exit.
The actual webbing passes through the slot using permitted actions without forced deformation.

steps.recoveryHint: Withdraw only the free end to the last confirmed slot, expose the face mark and rethread that segment.

steps.title: Expose the hidden return path
steps.instruction: Request the rear or underside view needed to inspect the return segment. Keep the unseen face unknown and identify the earliest slot responsible for a twist or wrong return.
visibleChecks: The requested return-side segment is actually exposed.
Its shown slot labels agree with the declared return path.
No visible fold or half twist contradicts the marked face route.

requiredConfirmations.label: I inspected the rear or underside route rather than assuming the front view proves it.
I checked the whole threaded path for twists and corrected any wrong return segment.

steps.recoveryHint: Back out to the first incorrect face transition. Preserve the confirmed upstream path and recheck the newly exposed rear segment.

steps.title: Review the tail and reversible operation

measurements.label: Actual free tail length after operation

steps.instruction: Inspect the final path and free end after the declared gentle operating motion. Request the actual tail-length reading; visible neatness is not a retention test.
visibleChecks: The shown final slot and free tail agree with the reference route.
The marked face remains consistent across the inspected segment.
The free end is accessible for the declared release action.

requiredConfirmations.label: I measured the actual free tail against the declared minimum.
I checked the prototype opening/release and reset using only permitted actions.

steps.recoveryHint: If operating the prototype pulls a tail through or introduces a twist, record that failure and recheck the affected path and tail reserve.

completionChecks: The declared front/back slot sequence is inspected on both sides.
Twists and wrong return paths are resolved rather than hidden.
Actual tail reserve, reversible operation and reset are operator-reviewed.
limitations: The camera cannot establish friction, tensile strength or secure retention.
An unseen rear path cannot pass from front-view evidence alone.
This profile does not validate lifting, climbing, restraint or personal-support equipment.

facts.declared_slot_path: Synthetic reference: W2 front entry, W8 rear return, W5 front entry.
facts.slot_labels: Synthetic W2, W8, W5, FRONT and FREE END.
facts.front_face_marker: Synthetic blue line marks the webbing front; FRONT marks the board.
facts.operator_constraints: Hypothetical right-hand non-loadbearing bench prototype; reversible threading only.
